passage: extracts class-like declarations from a php file using the tokenizer, so discovery can decide which fully qualified name to autoload without ever executing an unknown file directly.
providers are the only code discovery executes; they must be pure and are held to a per-provider time budget.
key derivation: printable string keys are used as-is, integer keys become "#<value>", and empty or non-printable string keys become the first eight hex characters of the key's sha-256 hash.
undecodable cached payload; treat as a miss and re-parse.
fromdecoded() validates untrusted json and returns null when any part of the shape is malformed, so a corrupt cache degrades to a re-parse. jsonserialize() emits the same shape.
discovery never silently skips a file it cannot resolve; every failure mode has a named constructor whose message identifies the file, class, or method involved.

acceptsid() applies the id filters after data-set expansion, against the rendered test id (class::method, with the data-set label when present), case insensitively, with the same substring-or-wildcard rule; exact ids match the rendered id verbatim.
include lists are or-ed within a dimension and and-ed across dimensions; exclude lists always win.

class-level attributes merge into each method: the method-level value wins on conflict, groups merge as a union (class groups first), and isolation applies when either level declares it.
default order is file path order; a seed shuffles the class order deterministically. methods always keep declaration order within a class, and data sets keep provider order within a method.

resolves the class declared in a file without executing the file: token parsing yields the expected fully qualified name, autoloading then loads exactly that class, and reflection confirms the class really came from this file.
